Bulgaria has changed its position on a proposed €45 billion EU loan for Ukraine but will not contribute to funding weapons purchases, Reuters reports. Speaking at an EU summit in Brussels, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said Sofia was prepared to help finance Ukraine’s civilian needs. “There is a large, historic Bulgarian diaspora living in Ukraine, and we would like to focus our support specifically in that area. We will make a contribution, but no money from Bulgaria will go toward weapons,” he said. The European Commission has proposed allocating €25 billion of the loan to Ukraine’s military needs and €20 billion to civilian needs. Hungary, Slovakia, and the Czech Republic currently oppose the proposal. It requires the support of all EU member states to be approved.
